verdictBasis: REJECT: 1 blocker, 2 SHOULD-FIX. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. The two frozen Codex v6 findings are substantively repaired and OBL-1 through OBL-5 all pass. Every finding below is in appliesFindingsOf or its schema residue, not in the projection law: the artifact pins my frozen v5 verdict by digest and then misstates its contents, mischaracterizes CLAUDE-V3-S1 while re-committing it, and leaves the not-produced arm's own enum admitting a value the same arm forbids for every standing.
role: independent; refute not confirm; authored none of v1-v7
measurementTool: python3 hashlib.sha256 over open(p,'rb').read(); mode via os.stat/stat.S_IMODE
priorInvolvementDisclosure: I authored the Claude 2 independent reviews of v2 (ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES — wrong; both Codex v2 findings were real), v3 (REJECT) and v5 (REJECT). v7 folds CLAUDE-V5-S1, my own finding, and CLAUDE-V7-B1 concerns how v7 records my own v5 verdict. I state the conflict plainly and have confined both to facts anyone can re-derive in one command: the advisory list inside a file v7 pins by digest, and the title and location of a finding inside a file frozen at 0444. I did not author the Claude v6 review on disk and did not read it.

claudeV6ReviewNotRead.disposition: Measured, not opened. v7's notFoldedThisSuccessor[0] says 'Claude v6 review was in flight at authoring; findings beyond CODEX-V6-B1/S1 require a v8.' Its mode 0644 is consistent with in-flight and unfrozen. I did not author it, the dispatch does not pin it, and nothing in my findings depends on its contents.

blockers.title: The artifact pins the frozen Claude v5 REJECT by digest and then misstates its contents, erasing four advisories from the ledger
detail: appliesFindingsOf.claude2v5 records the Claude v5 verdict as {verdict: REJECT, blockers: [], shouldFix: [CLAUDE-V5-S1], advisories: []} at sha256 4637778d9267a7821fdcb4b2edd51c2c4ea42299ba7b86b542a1297e705f39f3.

The pin, the verdict, the empty blocker list and the single shouldFix are all correct — I re-measured the file and it reproduces at that digest, mode 0444. The advisory list is not. That file carries advisoryCount 4 and advisories ADV-SPC-V5-01, ADV-SPC-V5-02, ADV-SPC-V5-03 and ADV-SPC-V5-04. Recording [] is a false statement about bytes this artifact itself pins, checkable in one command.

The consequence is not cosmetic. Because the pin says there are no advisories, the four never reach notFoldedThisSuccessor either, so they leave the ledger entirely. The same list demonstrates the artifact knows how to carry unfolded advisories forward: notFoldedThisSuccessor[1] reads 'Claude v2 advisories ADV-SPC-V2-01/02/03 remain not folded.' The v5 advisories get no equivalent line.

At least two of the erased advisories are still live against v7's own bytes. ADV-SPC-V5-03 (COORD pin stale) is confirmed below at a now-larger append. ADV-SPC-V5-01 (reviewGuidance still instructing reviewers to attack the removed FC-NONAUTH ID) is unchanged in v7 at three entries.

For contrast, the sibling pin is accurate: codexv6 records blockers [SARIFV6-B1], shouldFix [SARIFV6-S1], advisories [], and the frozen Codex v6 verdict does carry advisoryCount 0. The defect is specific to the claude2v5 record, not a systematic convention.
blockers.whyBlockerGrade: CLAUDE-V5-S1 — the finding this section is repairing — was that the fold ledger misstated a prior reviewer's verdict and silently dropped its advisories. v7 repairs the identifier half of that finding and, in the same object, commits the same class of error again against a different verdict. A successor that pins evidence by digest and then misreports what the evidence says fails the evidentiary contract the whole chain rests on, and it fails it inside the repair claimed to cure exactly that failure. I would rate a wrong advisory list on an unpinned reference a SHOULD-FIX; on a digest-pinned frozen verdict, inside the claimed repair for a finding about this very defect, it is a blocker.
blockers.minimumRepair: Set claude2v5.advisories to [ADV-SPC-V5-01, ADV-SPC-V5-02, ADV-SPC-V5-03, ADV-SPC-V5-04] and add a notFoldedThisSuccessor line recording them as not folded, in the form already used for the Claude v2 advisories. Do not fold them into v8 substantively unless intended — recording them as outstanding is what is owed.

shouldFix.title: CLAUDE-V3-S1 is written off under a description that is not what it says, and v7 re-commits it by dropping v6's codexv5 pin
detail: notFoldedThisSuccessor[2] reads in part: 'CLAUDE-V3-S1 was the open v3 remainder folded as the v4/v5 claimed native/input work and is not re-opened here.' CLAUDE-V3-S1 is not native or input work. In the frozen Claude v3 REJECT at 506237dd…, mode 0444, its title is 'v3 drops v2's frozen-verdict pin and now carries no digest for any folded verdict' and its location is /appliesFindingsOf. The native and input work was CLAUDE-V3-B1 and CLAUDE-V3-B2, which the same sentence already accounts for separately and correctly.
So the sentence discharges a finding about verdict pins by attributing it to repairs that had nothing to do with verdict pins, and then closes it with 'is not re-opened here.'

It is also not true that the underlying defect is behind us. v6's appliesFindingsOf pinned codexv5 at 736e1f3aeff092b1045bcdd4890bb1dc8b6ecbc9434647048da47c9da222579d. v7 does not carry that pin. The pattern CLAUDE-V3-S1 named — each successor deleting its predecessor's frozen-verdict pin — recurs here for the third time I have measured it: v3 dropped v2's codexv1, v5 dropped v4's codexv2, v7 drops v6's codexv5.

This is genuine progress in one respect and I record it: v7 carries two pins rather than one, codexv6 and claude2v5, which is the first time this chain has pinned both reviewers of a generation. That is the right direction; it is the deletion of the inherited pin and the false discharge narrative that remain.
shouldFix.notEscalated: Kept below blocker because, unlike CLAUDE-V7-B1, no statement here misreports the contents of a file the artifact pins — the mischaracterization is of a finding in a file v7 does not pin, and the pin deletion is a continuity gap rather than a falsehood.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Restate notFoldedThisSuccessor[2] to describe CLAUDE-V3-S1 by what it says — verdict-pin continuity in /appliesFindingsOf — and record it as still open rather than folded. Then either carry codexv5 alongside codexv6 and claude2v5, or state the governing rule explicitly, e.g. 'each successor pins only the verdicts it folds; earlier pins are recovered from the predecessor generation', which would close CLAUDE-V3-S1 honestly for every future successor at once.

shouldFix.title: The not-produced arm's own enum still admits advertisement=sarif, which the same arm forbids for every DR-006 standing
detail: inputNotProduced.properties.advertisement.enum is ['none', 'sarif']. The same object's forbids clause states 'advertisement=sarif is forbidden on this arm for every DR-006 standing. sarif+INACTIVE is invalid-advertisement, not a not-produced reason.' There is no standing under which the enum's second member is reachable, so the arm declares a value its own rule makes dead.

I probed it rather than argued it. The record {variant: 'not-produced', advertisement: 'sarif', dr006Standing: 'INACTIVE'} passes the arm's JSON-Schema portion — required members present, variant matches the const, both values inside their enums. It is then rejected three separate ways: it is absent from lawfulCombinations, the forbids clause names it, and inputOutcomeLaw carries no sarif+INACTIVE row while invalidAdvertisement declares it a failed golden.

The outcome is therefore deterministic and Codex's SARIFV6-B1 impact — that OBL-1 and OBL-3 were not jointly deterministic — is genuinely cured. What remains is that a validator executing the declared schema admits a record only the prose rejects, in a contract whose last four blockers were all some form of declared schema contradicting declared rule (SARIFV2-B1, CLAUDE-V3-B1, SARIFV4-B1, SARIFV6-B1). The dispatch's own attack line is 'A lawful not-produced arm that still permits advertisement=sarif', and structurally the arm does still permit it.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Narrow the enum on this arm to ['none'], which makes the schema agree with forbids, lawfulCombinations and inputOutcomeLaw at once. If the broader syntactic domain is wanted so that an invalid-advertisement negative can be expressed as an input at all, keep the enum and add an explicit structural constraint on the arm rather than leaving the prohibition in prose only.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V6-B1 — inputOutcomeLaw legalized sarif+INACTIVE as a lawful not-produced state with reason dr006-inactive, contradicting applicability
repairVerification.disposition: REPAIRED IN SUBSTANCE — VERIFIED; one structural residue remains (CLAUDE-V7-S2)
howIChecked: inputOutcomeLaw.table now has exactly two rows: advertisement none with dr006Standing 'INACTIVE or ACTIVE' mapping to variant not-produced and expectedReason preview-not-advertised; and advertisement sarif with dr006Standing ACTIVE mapping to variant produced with expectedReason null and a real-64-hex requirement marked preview-blocked. There is no sarif+INACTIVE row at all — I filtered the table for one and got an empty list.

inputOutcomeLaw.invalidAdvertisement states the case explicitly and in the terms Codex's minimum repair asked for: sarif with INACTIVE 'is not a lawful not-produced reason. It is an invalid-advertisement negative … a failed golden, not preview-not-advertised and not dr006-inactive.' inputOutcomeLaw.forbidden adds 'variant=not-produced with advertisement=sarif (any standing). The only not-produced lawful advertisement is none.'

inputNotProduced.lawfulCombinations reduces to a single entry, advertisement none over both standings with expectedReason preview-not-advertised. The dr006-inactive reason is no longer reachable from any lawful not-produced combination, which is what made Codex's contradiction with applicability bite.
inputProduced.requiresLaw confirms the other side: sarif+ACTIVE with a real pin is the only produced state and 'This arm is unavailable in preview because preview advertisement is NONE.'
Both preview fixtures still validate: schema-valid against the arm, lawful under lawfulCombinations, reason matching the bound expectedReason, and zero 64-hex tokens anywhere in either fixture.

repairVerification.finding: CODEX-V6-S1 — native related-URI order was derived from opaque artifactRefs with no ref-to-URI association
howIChecked: nativeMappings[0] gains hostLocationList, named hostLocationEntries, described as an ordered host list owned by the host canonical result with the disclaimer 'This contract does not mint artifact-ref recipes.' Its entry shape binds exactly the three things Codex asked for: artifactRef as the opaque host identity, locationUri as an optional NFC URI 'when the host already has one', and role as primary or related.

orderLaw states 'relatedLocations preserve hostLocationEntries order among entries whose role is related and whose locationUri is present. The primary is excluded by entry identity (artifactRef), not by string-compare of opaque refs to URIs.' That is Codex's minimum repair almost verbatim, and it directly answers the dispatch attack 'relatedLocations ordered by comparing opaque artifactRefs to URIs'.

placementRule is rewritten to consume that list: for each result r, take hostLocationEntries in listed order, write the unique primary entry with a locationUri only at run.results[r].locations[0], write each subsequent related entry that has a locationUri at run.results[r].relatedLocations[k] for k=0..n-1 in the same list order, one URI per role per result, and entries without a URI are omitted from the native arrays and remain in opensip.artifactRefs. The result index r and the location indices are distinct, and the ordering source is no longer artifactRefs.
This also closes the residue I raised at v5 as ADV-SPC-V5-02, where placementRule fixed roles but left k unordered. It is now ordered by an authoritative host list.

repairVerification.finding: CLAUDE-V5-S1 — the fold ledger recorded a frozen Claude v3 REJECT under Codex's identifier namespace, treated an unfrozen PENDING review as frozen, and dropped both an open finding and a set of advisories
repairVerification.disposition: PARTIALLY REPAIRED — two of four parts fixed, two not; see CLAUDE-V7-B1 and CLAUDE-V7-S1
howIChecked: Part (a), identifier namespace: FIXED. notFoldedThisSuccessor[2] now says 'Claude v3 REJECT identifiers: CLAUDE-V3-B1/B2 …', using Claude's own namespace instead of SARIFV3-*. idCollisionNote correspondingly reads 'Codex v6 used SARIFV6-B1/S1. Qualify CODEX-V6-*. Claude v5 used CLAUDE-V5-S1.'

Part (b), the unfrozen Codex v3 review: FIXED. The same sentence records 'Codex v3 remained PENDING/IN-PROGRESS (mode 0644) with no frozen digest asserted', which matches what I measured at v5 and is the honest standing.
Part (c), CLAUDE-V3-S1 left open and the deleted predecessor pin: NOT FIXED, and mischaracterized. See CLAUDE-V7-S1.

Part (d), advisories omitted from the ledger while the v2 advisories are listed: NOT FIXED, and made worse — v7 now also erases the four Claude v5 advisories by recording them as [] on a pinned verdict. See CLAUDE-V7-B1.

Both architecture pins reproduce against live bytes at HEAD 9b06a2f. Line 304 is the sole line beginning '| DR-122 |' and is byte-identical to rowVerbatim. The 26 carried file-01 lines equal live lines 108-133 exactly. nonAuthority.verbatim is genuinely verbatim in file 01.

obligationReview.reason: Preview applicability is NONE, and the outcome law no longer legalizes a preview SARIF advertisement — the contradiction Codex scored at v6 is gone. CLAUDE-V7-S2 is a schema-declaration residue, not a live admissibility hole.

The member map, requiredness, cardinality and version behavior are intact, and the native surface is now fully determined: distinct result and location indices, primary at locations[0], related ordered by an authoritative host entry list, one URI per role, per-entry NFC. This obligation carried a SHOULD-FIX at v6 and I find it discharged.

One tagged rule governs each golden, both shipped goldens validate against their arm and bind the correct reason, produced goldens stay honestly parked on ID-DEP-S1 with no fabricated digest, and the ref-to-URI ordering bridge Codex found undefined is now defined. This obligation was FAIL-BLOCKER at v6 and I find it discharged.

coordinatorNote: The projection law is done. Both frozen Codex v6 findings are genuinely repaired, all five obligations pass for the first time in this chain, and the native surface and golden law are now fully determined — v8 should change nothing in machineSurface beyond narrowing one enum. Everything blocking acceptance is in appliesFindingsOf: correct claude2v5.advisories to the four ADV-SPC-V5-* identifiers it actually carries and record them as not folded in the form already used for the v2 advisories; restate CLAUDE-V3-S1 by what it says (verdict-pin continuity at /appliesFindingsOf) and record it open rather than folded as native/input work; carry codexv5 alongside codexv6 and claude2v5, or declare the pin-only-what-you-fold rule explicitly and close that finding permanently; and narrow inputNotProduced.properties.advertisement.enum to ['none'].
bindsTo: NOTHING. This is one reviewer's independent verdict. It does not mark DR-122 SATISFIED or QUALIFIED, does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/, does not resurrect G17, does not advertise SARIF in preview, does not mint RunId/Finding/D9 recipes, does not edit the subject, file 08, or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, and does not commit.
summary: REJECT at 1 blocker and 2 SHOULD-FIX, none of them in the projection law. Both frozen Codex v6 findings are genuinely repaired: sarif+INACTIVE is gone from every lawful combination and from the outcome table and is named an invalid-advertisement failed golden, with sarif+ACTIVE still the sole produced state and still preview-blocked; and nativeMappings now carries hostLocationEntries binding each opaque artifactRef to an optional NFC locationUri and a primary-or-related role, with relatedLocations preserving that list order and the primary excluded by entry identity rather than by string-comparing refs to URIs. All five obligations pass for the first time in this chain, the v6-to-v7 leaf diff puts zero of 56 changed, added or removed paths outside the roster, both architecture pins reproduce at HEAD 9b06a2f, line 304 is byte-identical and unique, and no recipe, D9 code, preview advertisement, G17 resurrection or positive authority appears anywhere. What fails is the ledger. appliesFindingsOf pins my frozen v5 REJECT at the correct digest and then records its advisories as [] when the file carries four, erasing ADV-SPC-V5-01 through 04 from the accounting — a false statement about bytes the artifact itself pins, inside the repair claimed for CLAUDE-V5-S1, which was a finding about exactly this defect. The same section writes off CLAUDE-V3-S1 as 'folded as the v4/v5 claimed native/input work' when its title is 'v3 drops v2's frozen-verdict pin and now carries no digest for any folded verdict', and then re-commits it by dropping the codexv5 pin v6 carried. And inputNotProduced still lists 'sarif' in the advertisement enum its own forbids clause rules out for every standing — closed three ways in prose, open one way in schema.
verdictStatement: This independent review rejects sarif-projection-contract.v7 at the measured subject digest and HEAD 9b06a2f. It does not apply or seal the candidate, change the DR-122 register standing, advertise preview SARIF, resurrect G17, mint Run/Finding/D9 recipes, or authorize docs/v2/implementation/.
